minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission worked through a heavy slate of hearings, mostly small residential projects, approving a Highland Street septic, a Sunset Lane dock and stairs, a dock-awning roof and a restaurant-to-dispensary redevelopment, and continuing most others to July 20. Discussion of a Hickory Hills Lake management plan and a retroactive driveway paving request drew the most debate. The commission also approved several small spending items from the timber rights fund and reported a large expected bequest.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a negative determination for a septic replacement at 216 Highland Street.
It approved a negative determination with conditions for a dock and stairs at 205 Sunset Lane: removable dock, two trees, no parking.
The Hickory Hills lake management plan was continued to July 20; the association will send revised conditions and the administrator and chair will draft their own.
The commission voted to pursue progressive enforcement, with enforcement orders for three properties and a fourth moved to an order.
It approved a timber rights fund expense for an engineered driveway plan on Howard Street, plus two GIS payments for trail mapping.

why_it_matters: Wetland permits for docks, driveways and septic work decide what a neighbor can build near water, and most of this slate was continued, so those decisions are still open.
The timber rights fund, not the tax levy, paid for the driveway engineering and trail mapping approved here, and an expected bequest for conservation land would add to the commission's money.
watch_next: July 20 meeting: continued hearings including Hickory Hills lake management, 509 Townsend Harbor Road and the McSweeney filings, plus draft lake conditions.
Election of officers, deferred until the full board is present.
